title: Break area reset: sequence, touchpoints and floor
audience: Cleaners who service staff kitchenettes and break rooms in offices, commercial buildings and shared sites.
learningOutcomes: Sequence the break-area clean so that surfaces are finished once and not re-soiled by later work.
Identify the touchpoints and the food-contact areas that need attention in every break-area visit.
Carry out the floor stage correctly, including moving furniture and protecting the finished floor.

instruction.heading: Think about how food and people use the room
instruction.body: A break room collects food residue, crumbs, spills and handprints. Cabinets, appliance doors and the sink take the most soil from food handling, while light switches, door handles and the fridge handle take the most contact. Plan the clean around those two patterns. The work is not only about looking clean. Food residue left on cabinet faces or in the sink basket attracts pests and odour, so those areas need the same care as the floor.

instruction.heading: Start with the waste and the consumables
instruction.body: Before you wipe anything, empty the bin. Take out the full bag, then seat a new liner snugly over the rim so it stays put when waste is dropped in. Refill paper towel, hand soap and any other consumables. Doing this first stops food waste from dropping onto surfaces you have already cleaned.

instruction.heading: Work the room in a steady loop
instruction.body: Move through the room in one direction so that you never walk back over finished work. Start on the far side from the exit and work toward the door. Dust the high surfaces first with an extension duster, then change to a dry cloth for the lower dusting. At the sink, sanitiser goes on a sanitiser to one cloth and wipe the cabinet fronts, handles, the counter and the splashback, then rinse the cloth and wipe any overspray off nearby walls and objects. Move on to the touchpoints. Clean the fridge, dishwasher and microwave exteriors, and the exterior of the stove, using the cloth colour set for those zones.

instruction.heading: Polish the sink and the floor
instruction.body: Polish the sink last, because the splashes from the earlier work will mark it. A stainless steel sink can be polished with a steel-appropriate product, and a glass cleaner can be used on the taps and the chrome around the sink. Once the upper zones are finished, move the furniture out of the way of the mop and the vacuum. Move the floor mats out of the area and set up a wet floor sign by each entrance. Clear chairs away from the tables so that the floor under and around them can be reached. Begin on the far side and mop back toward the exit, so you never step onto the section you have just washed. Once the floor has dried, remove the sign and return the mats and chairs to their positions.

procedure: Put on gloves and eye protection before you begin.
Empty the bin and seat a new liner snugly over the rim, so it stays put.
Refill paper towel, hand soap and other consumables.
Dust the high surfaces with an extension duster, then dust the lower surfaces using a dry cloth, working from the far side toward the door.
At the sink, wipe the cabinet fronts, handles, counter and splashback with a sanitiser on one cloth, and wipe any overspray off walls and objects.
Clean the touchpoints, including switches, handles and push plates, and the exterior of the fridge, dishwasher, stove and microwave.
Polish the sink with the product suited to its finish, then polish the taps.
Move mats out, set up wet floor signs, and pull the chairs back from the tables.
Vacuum or sweep the floor, paying attention to corners and under the tables.
Mop from the far end toward the door, working around the table legs, then remove the sign once the floor has dried and return the mats and chairs.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner has finished wiping the cabinets and the splashback, but the bin liner has split and food residue has spilled onto the counter while the bin is being emptied.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the cleaner do next, and what should have been done earlier?
workedExamples.reasoning: The spilled residue has to be removed from the counter and the cabinet fronts re-wiped, because the spill landed on surfaces already finished. The bin should have been emptied and fitted with a secure liner before any wiping started. The other parts of the room should be checked for splashes before the floor stage.

workedExamples.situation: A break room has a stainless steel sink with a few water marks and a set of taps that look dull after the wet work.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: In what order should the sink and taps be treated?
workedExamples.reasoning: Wipe the sink and taps during the wet stage first, then polish them last. The sink gets a product suited to stainless steel and the taps get a glass cleaner, so the polish sits on a clean, dry surface.

equipmentAndPpe: Extension duster and a dry cloth for dusting.
Colour-coded microfiber cloths, with one colour set aside for food-contact zones.
Sanitiser and a general-purpose cleaner, both approved for food-contact or kitchen-type surfaces as the site requires.
Stainless steel polish and a glass cleaner for the sink and taps.
Bin liners and paper towel and hand soap refills.
Microfiber flat mop, bucket or mop equipment, and a wet floor sign.
Vacuum or dust pan and broom for the floor.

commonErrors.error: Wiping the cabinets before the waste has been removed, so that spills land on finished surfaces.
commonErrors.prevention: Empty and reline the bin first, then start the wet work.

commonErrors.error: Using the same cloth on the food-contact zones and the touchpoints.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the colour-coded cloths as set for each zone, and swap to a clean cloth when it is soiled.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the chairs in place, so the floor under the tables is missed.
commonErrors.prevention: Move the chairs up to the tables during vacuuming, then clear the path for mopping.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Keep gloves on for the whole clean, and do not touch the face while working. Remove gloves before handling food items or personal belongings.
Set out a wet floor sign by each entrance during mopping, and keep it in place until the floor has dried.
Check the label or safety data sheet before using a sanitiser near food surfaces. Do not mix products.
Food handling rules that apply to a kitchen operator may be stricter than this lesson. Follow the site's food-safety instructions. This lesson does not set them out.

qualityStandard: Cabinet fronts show no food residue or crumbs, the counter or the splashback.
The bin is emptied and fitted with a secure liner.
Touchpoints, including switches, handles and push plates, are clean.
The sink is clean and polished, and the taps are bright.
The floor is clean, including corners and the area under the tables, and it is dry when the sign is removed.
Mats and chairs are returned to their positions.
documentationEvidence: Job record of the break-area service, with the date and time.
Note of any appliance, sink or tap that is damaged or needs repair.
Note of any consumables that were low or missing at the start of the visit.
summary: Empty the bin first, so food waste never lands on finished surfaces.
Work in a steady loop from the far side toward the door.
Clean the food-contact zones and touchpoints with the colour-coded cloths set aside for them.
Polish the sink and taps last, and end with the floor once the upper zones are dry.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is the waste removed before any wiping starts in a break room?
options: Because the bin must be empty before the sink can be polished and dried
So that spills from the bin do not land on surfaces that have already been cleaned
So that the mats can be taken out before the floor is vacuumed and cleaned outside

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are the sink and taps polished last?
options: Because polish must be left on overnight to work
Because the taps are cleaned with the floor mop in a separate step
Because the splashes from the wet work would mark a polish applied earlier

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct sequence for the floor stage?
options: Move mats out, set signs, pull chairs back, vacuum, then mop from the far end toward the door
Mop the floor first, then vacuum under the tables, then move the mats and then put the chairs back
Mop from the door toward the far end, then clear the chairs and then vacuum the mats
